arxiv-1510-05198.title: Learning Multi-faceted Representations of Individuals from Heterogeneous Evidence using Neural Networks
arxiv-1510-05198.creator: Jiwei Li, Alan Ritter, Dan Jurafsky
arxiv-1510-05198.description: Abstract Inferring latent attributes of people online is an important social computing task, but requires integrating the many heterogeneous sources of information available on the web. We propose learning individual representations of people using neural nets to integrate rich linguistic and network evidence gathered from social media.

arxiv-2302-04546.title: First Principles Theory of the Pressure Induced Invar Effect in FeNi Alloys
arxiv-2302-04546.creator: Amanda Ehn, Björn Alling, Igor A. Abrikosov
arxiv-2302-04546.description: Abstract The Fe 0.64 Ni 0.36 alloy exhibits an anomalously low thermal expansion at ambient conditions, an effect that is known as the invar effect. Other Fe x Ni 1-x alloys do not exhibit this effect at ambient conditions but upon application of pressure even Ni-rich compositions show low thermal expansion, thus called the pressure induced invar effect.

arxiv-2303-04176.title: Inducing Superconductivity in Bilayer Graphene by Alleviation of the Stoner Blockade
arxiv-2303-04176.creator: Gal Shavit, Yuval Oreg
arxiv-2303-04176.description: Abstract External magnetic fields conventionally suppress superconductivity, both by orbital and paramagnetic effects. A recent experiment has shown that in a Bernal stacked bilayer graphene system, the opposite occurs – a finite critical magnetic field is necessary to observe superconducting features occurring in the vicinity of a magnetic phase transition.

arxiv-2404-16805.title: Accelerated inference on accelerated cosmic expansion: New constraints on axion-like early dark energy with DESI BAO and ACT DR6 CMB lensing
arxiv-2404-16805.creator: Frank J. Qu, Kristen M. Surrao, Boris Bolliet, J. Colin Hill, Blake D. Sherwin, Hidde T. Jense
arxiv-2404-16805.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Frank J. Qu, Kristen M. Surrao, Boris Bolliet, J. Colin Hill, Blake D. Sherwin, Hidde T. Jense. The early dark energy (EDE) extension to Λ \Lambda CDM has been proposed as a candidate scenario to resolve the “Hubble tension”. We present new constraints on the EDE model by incorporating new data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) survey and CMB lensing measurements from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6 and Planck NPIPE data.

arxiv-2407-01257.title: uDistil-Whisper: Label-Free Data Filtering for Knowledge Distillation in Low-Data Regimes
arxiv-2407-01257.creator: Abdul Waheed, Karima Kadaoui, Bhiksha Raj, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed
arxiv-2407-01257.description: Abstract Abstract Recent work on distilling Whisper’s knowledge into small models using pseudo-labels shows promising performance while reducing the size by up to 50%. This results in small, efficient, and dedicated models. However, a critical step of distillation using pseudo-labels involves filtering high-quality predictions and using only those during training.

arxiv-2410-01161.title: Robust Quantum Gate Preparation in Open Environments
arxiv-2410-01161.creator: Luke S. Baker, Syed A. Shah, Anatoly Zlotnik, Andrei Piryatinski
arxiv-2410-01161.description: Abstract We develop an optimal control algorithm for robust quantum gate preparation in open environments with the state of the quantum system represented using the Lindblad master equation. The algorithm is based on adaptive linearization and iterative quadratic programming to progressively shape the control signal into an optimal form.

arxiv-2411-04596.title: The Impact of Semi-Supervised Learning on Line Segment Detection
arxiv-2411-04596.creator: Johanna Engman, Karl Åström, Magnus Oskarsson
arxiv-2411-04596.description: Abstract In this paper we present a method for line segment detection in images, based on a semi-supervised framework. Leveraging the use of a consistency loss based on differently augmented and perturbed unlabeled images with a small amount of labeled data, we show comparable results to fully supervised methods.

arxiv-2411-17978.title: Convergence of the inverse Monge-Ampere flow and Nadel multiplier ideal sheaves. Nikita Klemyatin
arxiv-2411-17978.description: Abstract We generalize the inverse Monge-Ampere flow, which was introduced in [ 9 ] by Collins, Hisamoto and Takahashi, and provide conditions that guarantee the convergence of the flow without a priori assumption that X X has a Kähler-Einstein metric.

arxiv-2412-19056.title: Disorder-induced Diffusion Transport in Flat-band Systems with Quantum Metric
arxiv-2412-19056.creator: Chun Wang Chau 1,3, Tian Xiang 1, Shuai A. Chen 1,2, K. T. Law 1
arxiv-2412-19056.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chun Wang Chau 1,3, Tian Xiang 1, Shuai A. Chen 1,2, K. T. Law 1. Our previous understanding of transport in disordered system depends on the assumption that there is a well-defined Fermi velocity. The Fermi velocity determines important length scales in the system such as the diffusion length and localization length. However, nearly flat band materials with vanishing Fermi velocity, it is uncertain how to understand the disorder effects and what quantities determine the characteristic length scales in the system.

arxiv-2510-21001.title: Grauert’s Approximation Theorem in any Characteristic and Applications
arxiv-2510-21001.creator: Gert-Martin Greuel, Gerhard Pfister
arxiv-2510-21001.description: Abstract Abstract In his seminal Inventiones paper from 1972 Grauert proved the existence of a semiuniversal deformation of an arbitrary complex analytic isolated singularity. For the proof he invented an approximation theorem for solving a system of ”nested” analytic equations, which is now called Grauert’s approximation theorem.

pmc-11429491.title: Modulation of Antioxidant Enzyme Expression of In Vitro Culture-Derived Reticulocytes
pmc-11429491.creator: Hannah D. Langlands, Deborah K. Shoemark, Ashley M. Toye
pmc-11429491.description: The regulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in red blood cells (RBCs) is crucial for maintaining functionality and lifespan. Indeed, dysregulated ROS occurs in haematological diseases such as sickle cell disease and β-thalassaemia. In order to combat this, RBCs possess high levels of protective antioxidant enzymes.

pmc-11494154.title: Associations Between Developmental Stability, Canalization, and Phenotypic Plasticity in Response to Heterogeneous Experience
pmc-11494154.creator: Shu Wang, Ragan M Callaway
pmc-11494154.description: The processes of developmental stability, canalization, and phenotypic plasticity have ecological and evolutionary significance, and been studied extensively, but mostly separately and thus the relationships between them are not straightforward. Our objective was to better integrate these processes in the context of temporally heterogeneous environments.

pmc-11980538.title: Automated quality control of small animal MR neuroimaging data
pmc-11980538.creator: Aref Kalantari, Mehrab Shahbazi, Marc Schneider, Adam C. Raikes, Victor Vera Frazão, Avnish Bhattrai, Lorenzo Carnevale, Yujian Diao, Bart A. A. Franx, Francesco Gammaraccio, Lisa-Marie Goncalves, Susan Lee, Esther M. van Leeuwen, Annika Michalek, Susanne Mueller, Alejandro Rivera Olvera, Daniel Pad
pmc-11980538.description: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a valuable tool for studying brain structure and function in animal and clinical studies. With the growth of public MRI repositories, access to data has finally become easier. However, filtering large datasets for potential poor-quality outliers can be a challenge. We present AIDAqc, a machine-learning-assisted automated Python-based command-line tool for small animal MRI quality assessment.

pmc-12401142.title: COPD in Brazil: where there’s smoke…
pmc-12401142.creator: Frederico Leon Arrabal Fernandes
pmc-12401142.description: ss components for heating, energy, and cooking. 1 , 2 This remains a common practice in rural areas and urban outskirts. 1 , 2 This environmental vulnerability is compounded by limited access to health care services, especially in rural and remote regions, where primary care infrastructure may be weak and access to complementary tests-particularly spirometry-may be virtually nonexistent.

pmc-12495763.title: Interplay of rice vitamin E under osmotic and extreme temperature stresses revealed by a comparative transcriptomic approach
pmc-12495763.creator: Sara Kazemzadeh, Naser Farrokhi, Asadollah Ahmadikhah, Pär K. Ingvarsson
pmc-12495763.description: BackgroundRice (Oryza sativa L.) is vulnerable to abiotic challenges. Understanding stress response mechanisms is therefore a priority for enhancing rice development. Tocopherol is a known antioxidant that helps plants adapt to various abiotic stresses. We analysed bibliographic data from 13 years of studies on abiotic stresses.

pmc-12650537.title: Does Resistance Indicate Malposition? A Standardized Comparison of Pedicle Screw Placement
pmc-12650537.creator: Sascha Kurz, Benjamin Fischer, Janine Schultze, Florian Metzner, Toni Wendler, Christoph-Eckhard Heyde, Stefan Schleifenbaum
pmc-12650537.description: Pedicle screw malpositioning remains a frequent complication, with reported rates from 2% to 15%, often leading to revision surgeries. Analyzing mechanical resistance and torque encountered during screw insertion has been implicated as a promising approach for real-time detection. Five fresh-frozen human thoracolumbar spine specimens were utilized in this study.

pmc-13235443.title: Protocol for the isolation of human buccal cells for single-cell applications
pmc-13235443.creator: Supranee Buranapraditkun, Pongsawat Rodsaward, Natcha Chottawornsak, Pattarawat Thantiworasit, Jongkonnee Wongpiyabovorn, Hiroshi Chantaphakul
pmc-13235443.description: SummaryHuman buccal mucosa contains epithelial, stromal, and resident immune cell populations, but isolating these cells as a high-viability single-cell suspension is technically challenging. Here, we describe a gentle dissociation workflow for human buccal punch biopsies that combines controlled enzymatic digestion (collagenase and nuclease) with optimized speed, temperature, and incubation time to efficiently release heterogeneous cell populations while minimizing cell damage.

pmc-13244212.title: Functional reorganisation of lingual gyrus mediates cognitive impairment in COPD: a multimodal neuroimaging study
pmc-13244212.creator: Tianlu Teng, Yu Zhang, Jingting Sun, Ziyi Jing, Ling Wang, Xuejing Li, Xiangming Li, Lucas Becker, Huan Ye, Zhenghan Yang, Zhenchang Wang, Qian Chen
pmc-13244212.description: BackgroundCOPD is a systemic disorder associated with cognitive impairment and affective dysfunction. However, the underlying neurobiological mechanisms remain unclear. This study examines brain reorganisation in patients with COPD and investigates potential neural mediators of cognitive and affective deficits.MethodsWe enrolled 51 COPD patients and 50 age- and sex-matched healthy controls.

pmc-13283666.title: Contralateral Lower Extremity Pain in Pediatric and Young Adult Sports Participants with Lower Extremity Amputation/Transverse Limb Deficiencies
pmc-13283666.creator: Mary Dubon, Vincent S Mosca, Maya Gopalan, Rebecca Siegel, Saurav Pandey, Sachin Pathangey, Corey Gill, Colleen Coulter, Jonathan Napolitano, Daryn Strub, Kirsten Tulchin-Francis, Phoebe Scott-Wyard, Jonathan Bean
pmc-13283666.description: Background:Contralateral lower extremity (LE) pain and osteoarthritis are common in adults with unilateral LE amputation, thought to be secondary to overuse. Contralateral LE pain in pediatric-onset LE amputation or transverse limb deficiency (“LE amputation”) is understudied. We suspect that this population also experiences contralateral LE pain.

pmc-13331075.title: Predicting health and disease: a conceptual framework for AI in preventive and precision medicine
pmc-13331075.creator: Anis Barmada
pmc-13331075.description: The conventional medical approach of treating symptoms as they appear with restricted screening often limits intervention to slowing disease progression rather than fully reversing it. A new approach leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) and computational technologies across expanding multimodal biomedical datasets holds the promise to enable predicting actionable future changes in health before symptom onset.

pmc-13430789.title: Trajectories of sickness absence in healthcare workers: a cohort study in a Spanish hospital between 2018 and 2023
pmc-13430789.creator: Carlos Lopez-Muley, Fernando G Benavides, José María Ramada, Consol Serra, Laura Serra, Mireia Utzet
pmc-13430789.description: BackgroundSickness absence (SA) is a key indicator of health and job performance. The COVID-19 pandemic increased workload and stress, potentially affecting healthcare workers’ (HCWs) health and retention. This study aimed at identifying vulnerable HCW groups by analysing SA trajectories before and after the pandemic.

pmc-13572605.title: Interparental conflict and adolescent online flaming: the chain mediating roles of psychological stress and online disinhibition
pmc-13572605.creator: Suizhi Zeng, Zhijun Liu, Lei Zheng
pmc-13572605.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the relationship between interparental conflict and online flaming among Chinese adolescents, to test the mediating effects of psychological stress and online disinhibition (including toxic disinhibition and benign disinhibition) in this relationship, and to further explore gender differences in these mechanisms.
